sources.title: AI-Powered Corporate Training Market Size, Share & 2031 Growth Trends Report
sources.claim: AI-Powered Corporate Training Market valued at USD 7.49 billion in 2026, growing at 19.43% CAGR to reach USD 18.19 billion by 2031. Market was USD 6.27 billion in 2025.

sources.title: New Research: How AI Transforms $400 Billion of Corporate Learning
sources.claim: The global corporate training market is $400B+. AI is restructuring all major L&D platforms — from content catalogs to personalized learning paths — making AI the dominant growth driver in the sector from 2025 onward.

sources.title: US Department of Commerce $25M AI Upskill Accelerator Pilot Program
sources.claim: EDA announced approximately $25 million in funding for the AI Upskill Accelerator Pilot Program in May 2026 — the first federal grant program dedicated to AI workforce training, using a sectoral partnership approach.

sources.title: AI Upskilling 2026: Stay Relevant as 80% Must Retrain
sources.claim: 80% of the global workforce must undergo some form of AI reskilling or upskilling within the next four years (WEF-sourced). Workers with AI proficiency earn on average 56% more than peers in comparable roles.

sources.title: AI Corporate Training Statistics 2026
sources.claim: Demand for AI literacy training increased 320% on corporate learning platforms in 2025. AI training technology vendors raised $5.3 billion in 2023, with 127% year-over-year investment growth vs 2022. 1 in 10 job postings now require AI skills.

sources.title: Workforce and Learning Trends 2026
sources.claim: 70% of organizations actively using AI (up from 63% in 2025). 85% of employers plan to prioritize reskilling and upskilling over hiring to meet AI-driven skill demand.

sources.title: Job Skills Report 2026 — Future Job Skills & AI Insights
sources.claim: AI literacy named #1 in-demand skill globally for 2026. 140+ Fortune 500 companies purchased Coursera enterprise AI training packages. University credential moat drives adoption in regulated industries.

sources.title: AI Growth Acceleration Versus Distributional Fairness
sources.claim: AI adoption distributional effects require parallel investment in workforce training to prevent widening skills inequality. Policy frameworks must address both AI acceleration and workforce transition simultaneously.

sources.title: Global Economic and Financial Implications of Artificial Intelligence
sources.claim: Under rapid AI adoption assumptions, US GDP could increase by approximately $2.48 trillion by 2030. AI should be treated as a macro-critical transition requiring coordinated workforce and fiscal policy responses.

sources.title: Corporate Reskilling 2026: The $215B EdTech Push
sources.claim: Global EdTech market valued at approximately $214 billion in 2026, projected to grow to $588 billion by 2034 at 13.5% CAGR. Corporate reskilling is the highest-growth segment of the global education economy in 2026.

sources.title: The Enterprise Learning Tech Market Quickly Transforms Around AI
sources.claim: All major L&D platform vendors (LinkedIn Learning, Coursera, Udemy Business, Degreed, Skillsoft, Pluralsight) have pivoted to AI-first feature sets in 2025-2026. The market is consolidating around platforms that offer skills intelligence plus AI-generated personalized paths.

sources.title: AI and the Future of Work in 2026: The WEF Report
sources.claim: WEF predicts 60% of all jobs will require significant AI skills by end of 2027. More than half the global workforce needs reskilling within four years. WEF names AI & Machine Learning Specialists as #1 fastest-growing role globally.
sources.note: Secondary source summarizing WEF data — directionally accurate but cross-check original WEF Future of Jobs report for exact figures

unverified_claims.claim: LinkedIn Learning holds ~25% enterprise market share by learner seat count
unverified_claims.note: No public enterprise L&D market share breakdown available for 2026. Estimate based on reported 22M+ enterprise learners and Microsoft 365's 300M+ seat distribution advantage. [unverified — internal estimate]

unverified_claims.claim: Workflow-embedded microlearning achieves 3x the completion rate of scheduled LMS courses
unverified_claims.note: Widely cited industry benchmark; attribution varies across vendors. Original source appears to be a Salesforce Trailhead internal study. Cross-check with Axonify and 360Learning published data. [partially verified]

unverified_claims.claim: AI-powered course content generation reduces authoring time from weeks to hours
unverified_claims.note: Specific timing claims (weeks to hours) sourced from vendor case studies (Synthesia, Articulate AI). Independent third-party validation not found. [unverified — directionally credible]
